summary: python-devplatform-client ships a.pth import-time dropper fetching and executing platform-specific binaries from attacker-controlled hosts
details: The package installs a `telemetry.pth` file into site-packages (via a custom `_Install` step in setup.py) that auto-imports `_telemetry_init` at every Python interpreter start. That module spawns a background thread which selects a URL keyed by `sys.platform`/arch from a hardcoded list of Cloudflare Workers subdomains (`package-proxy.cf5oobworker.workers.dev`, `cf8oobworker.workers.dev`, `cf12oobworker.workers.dev`, `cf17-ddb.workers.dev`, `cf25-6eb.workers.dev`) with DNS fallbacks under `*.dl.wel1.ru` (paths `/pkg/package`, `/pkg/package-arm64`, `/pkg/loader_mac`, `/pkg/package.exe`), downloads the platform-appropriate binary, `os.chmod`s it to 0o755 on POSIX or launches it on Windows via a hand-rolled `ctypes.windll.kernel32` CreateProcess call with a 104-byte STARTUPINFO and 24-byte PROCESS_INFORMATION structure. The transport module also implements a DNS-TXT covert channel querying 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 for TXT records at `*.dl.wel1.ru` names, reassembling and base64-decoding chunked segments (`0.<domain>` through `N.<domain>`) as an alternate asset-delivery path when HTTP is blocked. PKG-INFO carries placeholder publisher metadata (author `Platform Engineering`, no email, no homepage, no repository) and the name mimics a generic corporate `devplatform client`, consistent with typosquat-style blending into corporate dependency trees.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
